fields.subject: index_patient
fields.name: Skin-prick testing before maternal allergen exclusion

evidence.quote: Patient 1 presented at 3 months of age with severe, exudative eczema unresponsive to emollients, 1% hydrocortisone and fusidic acid. She was exclusively breastfed, with longstanding reflux and vomiting after feeds, for which her mother had excluded cow’s milk from her diet. The patient was referred to allergy, dietetics, and dermatology services, and her treatment was escalated to include Fucidin H and topical tacrolimus. On review at 9 months of age, there was some improvement in eczema control, but she remained predominantly breastfed with severe aversive feeding, despite thickeners and exclusion of allergens from her mother’s diet after skin prick testing. Her weight dropped below the 0.4th centile, and blood tests showed marked deficiencies of iron, vitamin D and sodium with severe hyperkalemia. Due to the acute electrolyte imbalance and failure to thrive, she was admitted for supplementation and nasogastric feeding. During her admission, the initial hyponatremia (129 mmol/L) and hyperkalemia (7.4 mmol/L) improved (Table 1), normalizing a few days after discharge. Her renal function and renal ultrasound were normal throughout with low urinary sodium concentration (8 mmol/L). A urinary steroid profile requested while she was hyponatremic showed features of PHA, with increases of aldosterone precursors, corticosterone and aldosterone metabolites, excluding all saltwasting forms of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) and aldosterone synthase deficiency. Further endocrine investigations were performed 2 months after discharge showing normal sodium and potassium levels with borderline high aldosterone level of 6,750 pmol/L (indicative age-related range <1,000 pmol/L), normal renin activity and improvement in eczema control (Table 1). At 20 months of age, her aldosterone had normalized, with no aversive eating symptoms, eczema flares occurring less than monthly and her weight tracking the 50th centile (Table 2).

Patient 1 presented at 3 months of age with severe, exudative eczema unresponsive to emollients, 1% hydrocortisone and fusidic acid. She was exclusively breastfed, with longstanding reflux and vomiting after feeds, for which her mother had excluded cow’s milk from her diet. The patient was referred to allergy, dietetics, and dermatology services, and her treatment was escalated to include Fucidin H and topical tacrolimus. On review at 9 months of age, there was some improvement in eczema control, but she remained predominantly breastfed with severe aversive feeding, despite thickeners and exclusion of allergens from her mother’s diet after skin prick testing. Her weight dropped below the 0.4th centile, and blood tests showed marked deficiencies of iron, vitamin D and sodium with severe hyperkalemia. Due to the acute electrolyte imbalance and failure to thrive, she was admitted for supplementation and nasogastric feeding. During her admission, the initial hyponatremia (129 mmol/L) and hyperkalemia (7.4 mmol/L) improved (Table 1), normalizing a few days after discharge. Her renal function and renal ultrasound were normal throughout with low urinary sodium concentration (8 mmol/L). A urinary steroid profile requested while she was hyponatremic showed features of PHA, with increases of aldosterone precursors, corticosterone and aldosterone metabolites, excluding all saltwasting forms of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) and aldosterone synthase deficiency. Further endocrine investigations were performed 2 months after discharge showing normal sodium and potassium levels with borderline high aldosterone level of 6,750 pmol/L (indicative age-related range <1,000 pmol/L), normal renin activity and improvement in eczema control (Table 1). At 20 months of age, her aldosterone had normalized, with no aversive eating symptoms, eczema flares occurring less than monthly and her weight tracking the 50th centile (Table 2).

evidence.quote: Patient 2 presented at 7 months with 24 hours of lethargy and vomiting after feeds. His eczema had been managed with emollients, 1% hydrocortisone and fusidic acid, and now appeared to be infected and exudative. Formula had recently been added to his diet, after 6 months of exclusive breastfeeding, with his mother following a vegan diet. His weight was below the 0.4th centile (21st at birth). Initial blood tests showed marked hyponatremia of 115 mmol/L and hyperkalemia of 6.4 mmol/L with normal renal function (Table 1). This was associated with aldosterone levels >40,000 pmol/L (indicative age-related range < 2,000 pmol/L) and an elevated plasma renin activity of 22.4 nmol/L/h (indicative agerelated range <11 nmol/L/hr). An elevated white blood cell count of 40.6×109/L (lymphocytes 17.9×109/L, eosinophils 13×109/L, no blasts) and thrombocytosis were also noted. Patient 2 was admitted for intravenous fluids given his hyponatremia and IV flucloxacillin for infected eczema. Dermatology optimized his steroid regimen, and an amino acid formula was started due to concerns regarding cow’s milk protein allergy (CMPA). He was discussed with endocrinology and discharged with a sodium of 131 mmol/L (sodium level at the point of discharge from admission). On review at 11 months, his eczema and weight had improved (Table 2) – skin prick testing showed sensitization to milk, nuts, lentils and coconut, and so continued exclusion of these foods was recommended. Repeat bloods showed complete resolution of the electrolyte disturbances and normalization of aldosterone and renin levels.

summary.text: A7-month-old boy developed24hours of lethargy/post-feed vomiting with suspected infected exudative eczema despite emollients,1%hydrocortisone and fusidic acid. Formula had recently supplemented6months of exclusive breastfeeding; his mother followed a vegan diet. Weight fell from21stcentile at birth(3.19kg) to<0.4th(4.34kg).

Initial sodium was115mmol/L, potassium6.4, aldosterone>40000pmol/L and renin22.4nmol/L/hr, with preserved renal function. WCC40.6×10^9/L included lymphocytes17.9 and eosinophils13, with no blasts; platelets784×10^9/L, albumin28g/L and totalprotein39g/L were recorded. IV fluids and flucloxacillin treated electrolyte disturbance/infected eczema, dermatology optimized steroids, and amino-acid formula addressed suspected CMPA. He left hospital with sodium131mmol/L.

At11months eczema and growth improved to8.68kg/21stcentile; sodium137, potassium4.1, aldosterone140 and renin1.2 showed biochemical recovery. Skin-prick testing showed milk/nut/lentil/coconut sensitization and continued exclusion was recommended. Sensitization is not expanded into proven clinical reactions. Urine subtable results belong to Cases1/3, not this child.

summary.text: A5-month-old boy presented with a week of cough, vomiting and lethargy after2months of worsening severe exudative eczema despite emollients,1%hydrocortisone and maternal dairy/soya exclusion. Weight was6.28kg(11thcentile). Initial workup showed metabolic acidosis, sodium121mmol/L, potassium6.3, WCC49.2×10^9/L with lymphocytes18.2/eosinophils19.7 and no blasts; albumin27g/L, totalprotein43g/L and platelets659×10^9/L were recorded. Renal function and ultrasound were normal. ED urine sodium was7mmol/L, osmolality270mmol/kg; steroid profiling resembled PHA but excluded salt-wasting CAH/aldosterone-synthase deficiency.

ED fluid bolus/maintenance and sodium3mmol/kg/day preceded ward endocrine measurements: aldosterone3360pmol/L and renin88.3nmol/L/hr. Admission treatment included IV antibiotics and potent topical steroids. Amino-acid formula supplemented breastfeeding for suspected CMPA; testing showed milk/nut/house-dust-mite sensitization, with possible delayed soya allergy and continued maternal exclusions. Mechanisms of extrarenal sodium loss remain proposed rather than directly measured.

Three months after discharge skin improved considerably and renin normalized. Table8-month measurements show sodium138, potassium4, aldosterone<240, renin0.9, WCC12.5 and platelets371×10^9/L; weight8.2kg at25th–50thcentile. Exact discharge date and synchronization of the table age with relative follow-up are not invented.
